title: Distributed Tracing for AI Agents Across Services and Queues
summary: Distributed tracing for AI agents: carry span context across HTTP, queues, Temporal and approval pauses so each agent run stays in one trace with one root.
body_markdown:
Distributed tracing for AI agents follows one run across the processes that execute it. Your API can finish successfully while its research worker appears in a separate trace, with no parent or session connecting the work. For a run where each step has one upstream caller, the target is one trace with one root span.


Laminar's Python and TypeScript SDKs do not inject or extract HTTP or queue context themselves. Unless another integration handles propagation, you must serialize the parent context, carry it across the boundary and restore it downstream. This guide covers tested HTTP, queue and approval-resume patterns, plus Temporal's documented integration. It also explains when you need W3C traceparent


alongside Laminar's context to include framework-generated spans.


*Illustrative: the application spans share one trace when each boundary carries context. Framework-generated HTTP spans may also need W3C propagation, as the HTTP example explains.*


## Why agent runs split into several traces#


Within a process, Laminar carries the current span across function calls, async code and threads. A separate worker cannot read that process-local context. The parent must travel through the HTTP request, queued message or stored state that starts its work.


OpenTelemetry instrumentation libraries usually handle propagation for ordinary HTTP requests. Queues and stored resumes need their own context handoff unless an integration provides it. Laminar's Temporal integration is one such exception.


The measurements below come from exported spans in ClickHouse on a local Laminar stack built from main on 2026-10-22, using Python lmnr


0.8.0 and TypeScript @lmnr-ai/lmnr


0.8.51. These results describe that SDK/backend combination, not every OpenTelemetry service or future Laminar version.


## The pattern: serialize, carry, restore#


Laminar.serialize_span_context()


returns a string containing the current span's trace id, span id, ancestor paths, and associated session id, user id and metadata. Downstream, deserialize it and pass the result as parent_span_context


when starting the application span. Spans created inside that context, including auto-instrumented LLM calls, nest beneath it.


The[continuing traces docs](https://laminar.sh/docs/tracing/structure/continuing-traces) recommend treating incoming context as untrusted input and failing open: missing or malformed context should not fail the work. Within one service, pass span objects rather than serializing them.


Every Python receiver below uses this helper, saved as context_utils.py


:


```text
from   lmnr   import   Laminar


def     restore_parent  (  raw  :     str     |     None  )  :
if     not   raw  :
return     None
try  :
return   Laminar  .  deserialize_span_context  (  raw  )
except   Exception  :
return     None


```


Install the Python packages with pip install lmnr fastapi uvicorn httpx celery


. Set LMNR_PROJECT_API_KEY


in every process, and keep context_utils.py


importable by each Python worker.


## HTTP: an API service calling a research worker#


The caller, api.py


, starts answer_question


and sends its context to a research worker in a separate process:


```text
import   httpx
from   lmnr   import   Laminar  ,   observe


Laminar  .  initialize  (  )


@observe  (  name  =  "answer_question"  ,   session_id  =  "sess-42"  ,   user_id  =  "user-7"  )
def     answer_question  (  question  :     str  )  :
headers   =     {  }
span_context   =   Laminar  .  serialize_span_context  (  )
if   span_context  :
headers  [  "X-Laminar-Span-Context"  ]     =   span_context
resp   =   httpx  .  post  (
"http://research-worker:9100/research"  ,
json  =  {  "query"  :   question  }  ,
headers  =  headers  ,
)
return   resp  .  json  (  )


if   __name__   ==     "__main__"  :
print  (  answer_question  (  "context propagation"  )  )
Laminar  .  flush  (  )


```


The worker, research_worker.py


, restores that context before starting its application span:


```text
from   fastapi   import   FastAPI  ,   Request
from   lmnr   import   Laminar  ,   observe
from   context_utils   import   restore_parent


Laminar  .  initialize  (  )
app   =   FastAPI  (  )


@observe  (  )
def     search_sources  (  query  :     str  )  :
return     [  f"source for   {  query  }  "  ]


@app  .  post  (  "/research"  )
async     def     research  (  request  :   Request  )  :
body   =     await   request  .  json  (  )
parent   =   restore_parent  (  request  .  headers  .  get  (  "x-laminar-span-context"  )  )
with   Laminar  .  start_as_current_span  (
name  =  "research"  ,     input  =  body  ,   parent_span_context  =  parent
)  :
sources   =   search_sources  (  body  [  "query"  ]  )
Laminar  .  set_span_output  (  sources  )
return     {  "sources"  :   sources  }


```


For a same-machine test, make research-worker


resolve to 127.0.0.1


. Start uvicorn research_worker:app --port 9100


, then run python api.py


.


The three application spans share one trace: answer_question


is the root, research


is its child, and search_sources


sits beneath research


. All three inherit sess-42


and user-7


, which keeps the worker's application spans visible when filtering by[session](https://laminar.sh/docs/tracing/structure/sessions) . Missing or malformed headers returned HTTP 200 in our tests, with research


starting a new root.


**The file above carries only Laminar context.** FastAPI 0.161.1 also emitted OpenTelemetry framework spans in our test. With only the Laminar header, its POST /research


span landed in a separate trace.


To include that framework span in the run, also add from opentelemetry.propagate import inject


to the caller and call inject(headers)


after setting the Laminar header. This tested dual-header variant produced one trace with one root. The FAQ explains its hierarchy and session-id limit.


### A TypeScript worker behind a Python API#


The Laminar header works across languages. Install @lmnr-ai/lmnr


with npm and run this worker.ts


with npx tsx worker.ts


, instead of the Python worker:


```text
import   http   from     "node:http"  ;
import     {   Laminar  ,   observe   }     from     "@lmnr-ai/lmnr"  ;


Laminar  .  initialize  (  )  ;


const     rankSources     =     (  query  :     string  )     =>
observe  (  {   name  :     "rank_sources"     }  ,     async     (  )     =>     [  `  ranked results for   ${  query  }  `  ]  )  ;


http  .  createServer  (  async     (  req  ,   res  )     =>     {
let   raw   =     ""  ;
for     await     (  const   chunk   of   req  )   raw   +=   chunk  ;
const   body   =     JSON  .  parse  (  raw  )  ;


const   header   =   req  .  headers  [  "x-laminar-span-context"  ]  ;
const   span   =   Laminar  .  startSpan  (  {
name  :     "research"  ,
input  :   body  ,
parentSpanContext  :     typeof   header   ===     "string"     ?   header   :     undefined  ,
}  )  ;
const   sources   =     await   Laminar  .  withSpan  (  span  ,     (  )     =>     rankSources  (  body  .  query  )  ,     true  )  ;


res  .  writeHead  (  200  ,     {     "content-type"  :     "application/json"     }  )  ;
res  .  end  (  JSON  .  stringify  (  {   sources   }  )  )  ;
}  )  .  listen  (  9100  )  ;


```


The Python answer_question


span remained the root, with TypeScript's research


and rank_sources


nested beneath it and session/user ids inherited. The third argument to withSpan


ends the span when the callback settles, including on rejection.


The TypeScript SDK handles malformed parent context itself. Our malformed-header requests succeeded and started new roots. A TypeScript caller serializes with Laminar.serializeLaminarSpanContext()


; the[context utilities reference](https://laminar.sh/docs/sdk/context-utilities) covers both SDKs.


## Laminar span context vs traceparent#


W3C Trace Context defines traceparent


as version-traceid-parentid-flags


. OpenTelemetry's default propagator injects and extracts it.


We tested four carrier/downstream combinations. Three used Laminar's SDK downstream; one used a plain OpenTelemetry SDK exporting to Laminar. The comparison tracks the application spans, excluding framework-generated telemetry. As the HTTP test showed, the Laminar header alone did not connect FastAPI's server span.


*Measured application-span results on the local 2026-10-22 stack, with lmnr 0.8.0 and @lmnr-ai/lmnr 0.8.51. Framework spans are outside this diagram's scope.*


Carrier Downstream service Stored application spans


Nothing Laminar SDK Two separate traces


traceparent


Laminar SDK Same trace id; research


is a second root; no downstream session/user


traceparent


Plain OpenTelemetry SDK Nested under the caller; no downstream session/user


X-Laminar-Span-Context


Laminar SDK One root; nested; session/user on all three application spans


A plain OpenTelemetry service that extracts traceparent


creates spans with the correct parent, and Laminar preserves that nesting. Laminar's SDK also builds ancestor paths from its own context. With a bare traceparent


, it started a fresh path in our test, and the backend stored research


as a second root.


Neither traceparent


case carried session id, user id or trace metadata downstream. The header has no fields for those values, and we propagated nothing else.


Use W3C propagation for plain OpenTelemetry services. Session/user filters will miss their spans unless you carry those values separately. Between Laminar SDKs, carry Laminar context; add traceparent


when other instrumentation also needs the standard context. Laminar's Temporal integration writes both and prefers Laminar context when restoring.


## Queues and background jobs#


For a queue, carry the serialized context as a task argument and restore it inside the task. In tasks.py


, triage_inbox


fans out one job per document:


```text
from   celery   import   Celery
from   lmnr   import   Laminar  ,   observe
from   context_utils   import   restore_parent


Laminar  .  initialize  (  )
app   =   Celery  (  "jobs"  ,   broker  =  "redis://localhost:6379/0"  )


@observe  (  )
def     summarize_document  (  doc_id  :     str  )  :
return     f"summary of   {  doc_id  }  "


@app  .  task
def     summarize  (  doc_id  :     str  ,   trace_context  :     str     |     None     =     None  )  :
with   Laminar  .  start_as_current_span  (
name  =  "summarize_job"  ,
input  =  {  "doc_id"  :   doc_id  }  ,
parent_span_context  =  restore_parent  (  trace_context  )  ,
)  :
Laminar  .  set_span_output  (  summarize_document  (  doc_id  )  )


@observe  (  name  =  "triage_inbox"  ,   session_id  =  "sess-queue-1"  )
def     triage_inbox  (  doc_ids  :     list  [  str  ]  )  :
for   doc_id   in   doc_ids  :
summarize  .  delay  (  doc_id  ,   trace_context  =  Laminar  .  serialize_span_context  (  )  )


```


The displayed configuration requires Redis running at localhost:6379


and its Celery transport dependencies, available through pip install "celery\[redis\]"


. Start celery -A tasks worker


, then call triage_inbox(\["doc-1", "doc-2"\])


from your application.


We tested the task code with Celery 5.6.3's filesystem broker, not the displayed Redis configuration. With the default prefork pool and two worker processes, the trace contained one triage_inbox


root, two summarize_job


spans and their two summarize_document


children. All carried sess-queue-1


.


The jobs started after the parent span ended and still nested correctly. A parent need not remain open for a child to attach to it.


With default batching and the worker kept running, spans exported within 20 seconds without flushing inside tasks. Flush before a short-lived process exits, including a producer that enqueues work and immediately stops. Avoid flushing every task in a busy worker; see[flushing and shutdown](https://laminar.sh/docs/tracing/structure/flushing-and-shutdown) .


### Fan-in and span links#


A batch containing messages from independent runs cannot give its consumer span multiple parents. OpenTelemetry's messaging conventions use span links to represent those relationships.


The Laminar backend we tested does not persist or display span links. If you need native links between a consumer and several independent producers, make link support a backend-selection criterion.


With Laminar, you can correlate manually: start the batch as a root and record upstream trace ids in metadata. This function assumes an initialized worker with Laminar


and restore_parent


imported, and your application's embed


function available:


```text
def     embed_batch  (  batch  :     list  [  dict  ]  )  :
contexts   =     [  restore_parent  (  m  .  get  (  "trace_context"  )  )     for   m   in   batch  ]
source_ids   =     sorted  (  {  str  (  c  .  trace_id  )     for   c   in   contexts   if   c  }  )
with   Laminar  .  start_as_current_span  (
name  =  "embed_batch"  ,   metadata  =  {  "source_trace_ids"  :     ","  .  join  (  source_ids  )  }
)  :
embed  (  [  m  [  "text"  ]     for   m   in   batch  ]  )


```


Our test skipped malformed and missing contexts and recorded both valid upstream trace ids. This[SQL editor](https://laminar.sh/docs/platform/sql-editor) query found the batch: SELECT trace_id FROM spans WHERE name = 'embed_batch' AND position(attributes, '<upstream trace id>') > 0


.


That is searchable metadata, not stored span links or parent-child edges.


## Temporal workflows#


Laminar's Temporal integration handles propagation between the client, workflow and activities. We did not test Temporal end to end here; this section follows Laminar's integration guide and source.


For Python lmnr


0.7.53 or later, Laminar.initialize()


instruments Temporal when temporalio


is installed. Initialize in both the starting process and worker before Client.connect


. For TypeScript @lmnr-ai/lmnr


0.8.28 or later, register Laminar's client, activity and workflow interceptors. The[Temporal integration guide](https://laminar.sh/docs/integrations/temporal) supplies complete examples.


Do not create spans in workflow code. Temporal replays workflows, and an open span cannot survive replay; put instrumented work in activities. A scheduled workflow has no caller span, so each scheduled run starts its own root.


## Human approval: resume from stored state#


If the starting process exits while waiting for approval, store its context beside the state you will resume. This approvals.py


implements both steps:


```text
import   sqlite3
import   sys
from   lmnr   import   Laminar  ,   observe
from   context_utils   import   restore_parent


Laminar  .  initialize  (  )
db   =   sqlite3  .  connect  (  "approvals.db"  )
db  .  execute  (
"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS approvals "
"(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, draft TEXT, trace_context TEXT)"
)


@observe  (  name  =  "draft_weekly_report"  ,   session_id  =  "sess-approval-1"  )
def     draft_weekly_report  (  approval_id  :     str  )  :
draft   =     "Revenue up 4% week over week."
db  .  execute  (
"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO approvals VALUES (?, ?, ?)"  ,
(  approval_id  ,   draft  ,   Laminar  .  serialize_span_context  (  )  )  ,
)
db  .  commit  (  )


@observe  (  )
def     send_report  (  draft  :     str  )  :
return     f"sent:   {  draft  }  "


def     resume_after_approval  (  approval_id  :     str  )  :
draft  ,   trace_context   =   db  .  execute  (
"SELECT draft, trace_context FROM approvals WHERE id = ?"  ,     (  approval_id  ,  )
)  .  fetchone  (  )
with   Laminar  .  start_as_current_span  (
name  =  "resume_after_approval"  ,
input  =  {  "approval_id"  :   approval_id  }  ,
parent_span_context  =  restore_parent  (  trace_context  )  ,
)  :
send_report  (  draft  )


if   __name__   ==     "__main__"  :
step  ,   approval_id   =   sys  .  argv  [  1  ]  ,   sys  .  argv  [  2  ]
if   step   ==     "request"  :
draft_weekly_report  (  approval_id  )
else  :
resume_after_approval  (  approval_id  )
Laminar  .  flush  (  )


```


Run python approvals.py request appr-7


, then python approvals.py resume appr-7


from the same directory so both processes use the same database.


In our separate-process test, resume_after_approval


started 20.5 seconds after the original root. It and send_report


nested beneath draft_weekly_report


, with the session id on every span. A corrupted stored context allowed the resume to complete as a new root.


The serialized context contains no timestamp or expiry field. That does not establish behavior for arbitrary pause lengths: we tested about 20 seconds, not hours or days. The earlier trace must also remain within your project's data retention. These measurements make no claim about trace-duration calculations or timeline rendering.


## How to verify one run has one root#


Start with a known run. Check that its entry span is the only top-level span and inspect the worker hierarchy in the span tree and[transcript view](https://laminar.sh/blog/transcript-view-agent-traces) . Compare expected work with exported spans: two jobs without retries should produce two summarize_job


spans. If retries occurred, account for the attempts.


Do not use session filtering as a completeness check. An orphaned worker trace may lose its session id and disappear from that view.


In the[SQL editor](https://laminar.sh/docs/platform/sql-editor) , a top-level span has a zero parent_span_id


. This query finds traces with multiple roots:


```text
SELECT   trace_id  ,
countIf  (  parent_span_id   =     '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'  )     AS   root_spans  ,
count  (  )     AS   spans
FROM   spans
WHERE   start_time   >     now  (  )     -     INTERVAL     1     DAY
GROUP     BY   trace_id
HAVING   root_spans   >     1


```


It caught our traceparent


-only Laminar SDK case. It cannot catch two separate, single-root traces. For that signature, search for worker entry spans that became roots:


```text
SELECT   trace_id  ,   start_time
FROM   spans
WHERE   name   =     'research'
AND   parent_span_id   =     '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'
AND   start_time   >     now  (  )     -     INTERVAL     1     DAY


```


This returned our no-header and traceparent


-only runs, but not the Laminar-context run.


Both queries have limits. The window must include the producer and slowest consumer. A worker root indicates a bug only if that entry point always belongs to an upstream run. Clean results do not prove that every expected span exported. For instrumentation fundamentals, see[OpenTelemetry for AI agents](https://laminar.sh/article/opentelemetry-for-ai-agents) .


## FAQ#


### Does Laminar propagate trace context over HTTP automatically?#


No. Neither Laminar SDK instruments HTTP clients, web frameworks or task queues, so neither adds a header to outgoing requests or reads one from incoming requests. Propagation is automatic within a process and across Temporal. Other libraries in your stack may still create spans: FastAPI 0.161's built-in telemetry produced server spans in our test. At every other boundary, add X-Laminar-Span-Context


yourself, as in the[continuing traces docs](https://laminar.sh/docs/tracing/structure/continuing-traces) .


### Can I send traceparent and the Laminar header together?#


Yes. In the tested dual-header HTTP variant, FastAPI's POST /research


and Laminar's research


were siblings beneath answer_question


. The framework span used W3C context; the application span restored Laminar context. Everything shared one root, but the framework server span still lacked a session id. One trace does not guarantee identical attributes on every span.


### What should I log when context restoration fails?#


Record the extraction failure without copying the raw context into logs or responses. The Python helper deliberately returns None


without logging; the TypeScript SDK logged a warning for malformed context. Missing, garbage and structurally invalid JSON headers all allowed our worker requests to succeed. See the fail-open guidance in[continuing traces](https://laminar.sh/docs/tracing/structure/continuing-traces) .


### Does trace metadata travel in the header?#


Yes. Session id, user id and trace[metadata](https://laminar.sh/docs/tracing/structure/metadata) are included in serialized Laminar context. Keep metadata small because it crosses each boundary with the request or message, and avoid forwarding sensitive values to less-trusted services. Treat incoming user/session ids as correlation data, not proof of identity or permission.


### Can an approval resume intentionally start a new trace?#


Yes. Start a new root rather than restoring the stored parent, then assign the same session id to group the runs. The documented Laminar.set_trace_session_id()


must run inside an active span context. A[session](https://laminar.sh/docs/tracing/structure/sessions) groups traces; it does not create a parent-child relationship between them.


### How do I trace a subagent running as a subprocess?#


The Python SDK reads LMNR_SPAN_CONTEXT


during Laminar.initialize()


. Set that environment variable to the parent's serialized context before launching the subprocess. With lmnr 0.8.0, our subagent nested correctly but did not inherit the session id. To set it explicitly, call Laminar.set_trace_session_id()


inside the subagent's first span. In-process subagents do not need this process-boundary handoff; see[tracing the OpenAI Agents SDK](https://laminar.sh/article/openai-agents-sdk-tracing) .
